text:
People in India are switching to UPI because paying becomes as easy as sending a message, and it costs most users nothing.

Not long ago, paying meant carrying cash, hunting for change, or typing long card and bank details. Now you scan a code or enter a phone number, type your PIN, and the money leaves your bank account in seconds. The same habit works at a tea stall, a big store and a bill payment page, so one app covers almost everything.

Three main reasons:

Quick and simple: Scan, tap, enter your PIN. No cards, no change, no waiting.
Free for most people: Paying shops or sending money to friends usually costs nothing, so there is little reason to go back to cash.
Accepted everywhere: It works with almost any bank account and any UPI app. Even the smallest shop can accept it with a printed QR code.

Cheap smartphones and mobile data helped too. Shopkeepers like it because the money lands straight in their account, with no cash to count or carry to the bank. Once a few people around you use it, it quickly becomes the normal way to pay.

Plan a 3 day trip to Jaipur for my parents
2:45 PM

Here's a relaxed 3 day Jaipur plan for your parents, with one main stop each morning and rest in the afternoon.

Day 1, Old city: City Palace, Jantar Mantar and Hawa Mahal in the morning. Lunch nearby, then a rest. In the evening, a slow walk and shopping at Johari Bazaar, with a rickshaw or cab between stops.
Day 2, Amer Fort: Go early, before the crowds and heat. A jeep takes you up to the fort, so there is no steep climb. Stop at Jal Mahal for photos on the way back. In the evening, Nahargarh Fort for the sunset view, or a rest at the hotel.
Day 3, Easy and local: Albert Hall Museum and Birla Mandir in the morning. Then Rajasthani thali for lunch, and buy blockprint fabrics and jootis before leaving.

Late October and November are pleasant in Jaipur. A hired cab for all three days saves your parents a lot of walking. Book Amer Fort and the City Palace tickets online to skip the queues.
